title: The maximal flat locally finitely presented base open commutes with fppf morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an open subspace $V\subseteq Y$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace], write $f_V:X\times_YV\to V$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Flatness and local finite presentation of algebraic-space morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There is a unique largest open subspace $W(f)\subseteq Y$ such that $f_{W(f)}$ is flat and locally of finite presentation: $f_{W(f)}$ has these properties, and any open $V$ for which $f_V$ has them is contained in $W(f)$. If $g:Y'\to Y$ is any flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces, not necessarily surjective, then, for $f':X\times_YY'\to Y'$, one has $W(f')=Y'\times_YW(f)$ as open subspaces of $Y'$. No finiteness, separation or reducedness hypothesis is imposed on $f,X,Y$ or $Y'$.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), with the property flat and locally of finite presentation and the fppf topology; target locality of these properties: Tags 041W (lemma-descending-property-flat) and 041T (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Write $P$ for the conjunction of flatness and local finite presentation. Let $\mathcal G$ be the family of open subspaces $V\subseteq Y$ for which $f_V$ has $P$. By the inclusion-preserving correspondence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], open subspaces are indexed by the set of open subsets of $|Y|$; thus this is a set-indexed family in the chosen universe, rather than a family of all maps into $Y$. The union $O=\bigcup_{V\in\mathcal G}|V|$ is open. The same correspondence gives the unique open subspace $W\subseteq Y$ with point set $O$, and each $V\in\mathcal G$ is contained in $W$.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), proof, specialized to flat and locally of finite presentation; Tags 041W and 041T for target descent.

proof.text: We show that $f_W$ has $P$. The opens $V\subseteq W$, $V\in\mathcal G$, cover $W$. Their inverse images $X_V\subseteq X_W$ cover $X_W$: on any scheme mapping to $X_W$ these are inverse image opens whose point sets cover, by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. An open inclusion is representable etale by the scheme tests of [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The restriction of $f_W$ to $X_V$ is the composite $X_V\xrightarrow{f_V}V\hookrightarrow W$, so it has both properties by composition in that calculus. Its source-open-cover criterion now gives both properties for $f_W$. This also handles $W=\varnothing$, when the source is empty and the criterion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), proof, specialized to flat and locally of finite presentation; Tags 041W and 041T for target descent.

proof.text: Every good open $V$ occurs in $\mathcal G$, so $V\subseteq W$. Step 2 shows that $W$ is itself good. Thus $W=W(f)$ has the required largest-open property. If $W_1,W_2$ both have it, goodness of $W_1$ implies $W_1\subseteq W_2$, and goodness of $W_2$ implies $W_2\subseteq W_1$; antisymmetry of subfunctor inclusion gives uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), proof, specialized to flat and locally of finite presentation; Tags 041W and 041T for target descent.

proof.text: Let $g:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ be flat and locally of finite presentation, and put $W^{\prime}=W(f^{\prime})$. The inverse image $H=Y^{\prime}\times_YW(f)$ is open by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. The restriction of $f^{\prime}$ over $H$ is the base change of $f_{W(f)}$, so it has $P$ by arbitrary-base-change stability in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Maximality gives $H\subseteq W^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), proof, specialized to flat and locally of finite presentation; Tags 041W and 041T for target descent.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion, restrict $g$ to $h:W^{\prime}\to Y$. Its open source inclusion is etale by [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests], so $h$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the etale implications and composition in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Consequently its point image $|I|=h(|W^{\prime}|)$ is open by [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open], and [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] supplies the corresponding open subspace $I\subseteq Y$ (only its open-subspace correspondence is used). By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $h$ factors as $q:W^{\prime}\to I\hookrightarrow Y$, and $W^{\prime}\times_YI\simeq W^{\prime}$. Thus $q$ is the base change of $h$ by $I\hookrightarrow Y$ and has $P$ by the same calculus. By its defining image, $q$ is surjective on point classes. The fibre-product point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] also gives this surjectivity after any scheme base change.

source.place: Tag 06R2 (lemma-largest-open-of-the-base), proof, specialized to flat and locally of finite presentation; Tags 041W and 041T for target descent.

proof.text: The base change of $f_I:X\times_YI\to I$ by the surjective flat locally finitely presented $q:W^{\prime}\to I$ is $(f^{\prime})_{W^{\prime}}$, since both fibre products parametrize a section of $X$ and a section of $W^{\prime}$ with equal image in $Y$. It has $P$ by definition of $W^{\prime}$. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent], in its explicit algebraic-space case, separately to flatness and local finite presentation. It gives $P(f_I)$; hence $I\subseteq W(f)$. Therefore $g(W^{\prime})\subseteq|W(f)|$. The open inverse-image and inclusion criteria of [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] give $W^{\prime}\subseteq H$. Together with Step 4 this proves the claimed equality of open subspaces. No surjectivity of $g$, or finiteness or separation of $f$, was used.

W : OpenSubspace Y, IsFlatLfpOverSubfunctor f.hom.hom W.val ∧ (∀ V : OpenSubspace Y, IsFlatLfpOverSubfunctor f.hom.hom V.val → V ≤ W) ∧ ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Y' ⟶ Y), MapIsFlat g → MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation g → ∃ W' : OpenSubspace Y', W'.val = W.val.preimage g.hom.hom ∧ IsFlatLfpOverSubfunctor (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom g.hom.hom) W'.val ∧ ∀ V : OpenSubspace Y', IsFlatLfpOverSubfunctor (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom g.hom.hom) V.val → V ≤ W'
